info.name: EDK-Enterprise-Deployment
info.description: Post-provisioning customer walkthrough for an EDK enterprise deployment hosted under one base domain: platform.<baseDomain> for the platform/operator plane and <tenantSlug>.<baseDomain> for tenant protocol routes plus protected administrative API paths. Install the license and complete platform setup in the Admin Console UI before running this collection; those setup steps are intentionally not modeled as Postman API calls. The collection targets gateway host/path routes only and never calls workload containers or runtime probes directly.

item.name: 00 Before You Start
item.description:
Use the Admin Console UI to install the license and complete platform setup before running this collection. This Postman collection starts after the platform is provisioned; it covers operator sign-in, tenant onboarding, runtime discovery, issuer/verifier configuration, credential issuance, status lists, DCQL binding, and verification.

The environment file has six values: baseDomain, tenantSlug, tenantName, operatorEmail, operatorPassword and tenantOwnerPassword. Every URL, host, DID and API base in the collection is derived from baseDomain and tenantSlug before each request, so changing those two is enough to point the whole collection at another installation or another tenant. Nothing the collection derives is written back to the environment.

Folders in order: sign in as the operator (01), register a tenant and discover its runtime (02), activate the tenant owner and obtain the tenant service token (03, 04), optional subtenants (05), the tenant's keys and DID (06), bringing your own KMS and certificates (07), KMS sharing from the platform (08), authorization servers and federation to an external OIDC provider (09), issuer branding and credential designs (10, 11), status lists and per-credential configuration (12, 13), hosted branding checks (14), issuance of SD-JWT VC, mdoc and W3C VCDM credentials by pre-authorized code, transaction code, pipeline and authorization code (15 to 20), DCQL queries and verification (21, 22), trust domains and trust lists (23), the KMS runtime API for keys, certificates and signatures (24), and the Developer Console policy (25). Folders marked optional need provider resources you own and ship disabled.
